entities.name: An-Nadhar bin Syamil
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
An-Nadhar bin Syamil, full name Abu ʾl-Ḥasan al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl al-Māzinī al-Tamīmī, was a pivotal Arab polymath of the early Abbasid Caliphate, flourishing in the late 8th and early 9th centuries CE until his death in 818 CE. Hailing from Marw in Khurasan (modern Turkmenistan), he became a leading figure in the intellectual circles of Basra and Baghdad, contributing profoundly to Arabic philology, lexicography, Hadith studies, and astronomy. His work represents a crucial period of Arabic linguistic codification and the integration of diverse knowledge streams, establishing foundational texts and methodologies that influenced Islamic scholarship for centuries. He is particularly renowned for his comprehensive approach to language, combining rigorous textual analysis with ethnographic observation of Bedouin speech.

Educated initially in Marw, al-Naḍr bin Shumayl moved to Basra, a vibrant center of learning, where he studied under prominent grammarians and Hadith scholars such as al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi and Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj. His intellectual prowess quickly established him as a master of Arabic language, Hadith, and poetry. He dedicated a significant portion of his life to collecting and systematizing rare Arabic vocabulary, particularly terms related to natural phenomena, flora, and fauna, directly from Bedouin informants in the deserts of Arabia. This meticulous fieldwork culminated in his monumental lexicon, *Kitāb al-Ṣifāt* (Book of Qualities), a work of immense scope that documented hundreds of specialized terms with their precise meanings and usage, often drawing parallels with classical Arabic poetry. He also transmitted numerous Hadith, playing a role in the preservation of prophetic traditions.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: An-Nadhar bin Syamil's *Kitāb al-Ṣifāt* became a foundational text for Arabic lexicography, directly influencing the structure and content of subsequent major dictionaries and systematizing linguistic knowledge for centuries. His Hadith transmissions also contributed to the authoritative collections of prophetic traditions.
